record.file_problem: The full article text is present. Some mathematical symbols and figure labels are garbled in the web extraction.
record.tranche_reason: It extends scaling observations to zero-shot LAMBADA evaluations on Pythia checkpoints, and derives a compute-optimal allocation under a separable-loss model; it does not reproduce the original pretraining-loss experiments.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own qualitative Pythia LAMBADA plots and an analytical compute-allocation derivation. The referenced Kaplan and Hoffmann results and other cited empirical findings are not rows. The synthetic extrapolation figure illustrates uncertainty but is not a result on actual pilot runs.
record.test_reason: This is an analytical technical note: it derives mechanisms (approximation rates, feature coverage, separable-loss allocation) under assumed forms and says empirical results are identified by their sources. Its only data figure (Fig. 1) redraws Pythia's public LAMBADA checkpoint evaluations as a qualitative illustration, with no numbers, uncertainty or test of any version. The V3 allocation is derived from an assumed Chinchilla-style separable loss, so it assumes the form rather than testing whether real models follow it. No version is tested by the study's own results.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly right but incomplete. The authors derive exponents from three mechanisms: local approximation error decaying as Ne^(-γs/d), feature coverage giving αD=(β−1)/ζ, and separable-loss optimization giving the N/D split and compute exponent αNαD/(αN+αD). They argue that a scaling exponent depends jointly on target, loss, data and architecture, and holds only over a fitted interval. They also treat apparent emergence as a possible artifact of nonlinear scoring, test-time search with verification limits, deployment crossovers from overtraining, and SE(3) dimension reduction for molecules. All of this is analytical; the empirical results they mention are cited from other work.
record.recipe_differences: The original sources report empirical language-model scaling experiments. This note is primarily an analytical technical note and includes qualitative plots based on public Pythia checkpoint evaluations; it does not reproduce the original controlled sweeps.

fits_no_version.finding: In a qualitative redraw of Pythia zero-shot LAMBADA loss, offset-subtracted token-budget slices align around one shared fit, and small models plateau with tokens while 12B keeps improving (Fig. 1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Illustrative reanalysis only: zero-shot LAMBADA loss on public Pythia checkpoints follows a shared offset-plus-power form across token budgets. No numbers are reported.

record.problems: The Pythia findings are qualitative in the extracted text, with no numeric loss values or empirical uncertainty estimates. The compute-allocation result depends on the assumed separable loss and fixed dense FLOP factor. The extrapolation illustration is synthetic, not a validation on larger actual runs.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were omitted. Cited empirical results and the synthetic extrapolation illustration were excluded because they are not findings from actual runs reported by this study.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining-loss sweep over N, D or C.
No fit on small runs checked against larger runs; Fig. 3 is synthetic.
Allocation exponents are derived under an assumed loss form; there is no empirical allocation fit and no Kaplan-vs-Hoffmann comparison.
Vision and molecular sections are analytical only; repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer are only cited.
Only qualitative redrawn Pythia LAMBADA curves; no test of downstream prediction from scale or loss. The emergence section is a toy q^r model.
Dependence on setup is argued from cited work and theory; no comparison of fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's labels are dropped. The V3 'supports' label rested on an analytical derivation under an assumed loss form. The V6 labels rested on qualitative redrawn Pythia curves. The V6 'limits_scope' label from small-model plateaus also misread a parameter bottleneck as a failure of downstream predictability.

versions.untested_parts: The Pythia plot measures zero-shot LAMBADA loss, not held-out pretraining loss; no empirical parameter, token, or compute sweep of held-out pretraining loss is reported.
No actual small-run fit is evaluated against held-out runs orders of magnitude larger. The extrapolation discussion is general and its plotted example is synthetic.

The allocation powers are derived conditionally for a separable loss with positive power-law terms and C = κND; the paper does not empirically test whether real models follow these allocations or compare Kaplan's and Hoffmann's fitted exponents.
No matched-parameter comparison of depth, width, or other architecture choices is reported.
Visual and molecular settings are treated analytically, not through empirical tests of whether the same measured loss laws hold; repeated-data, fine-tuning, and transfer are not tested.
The evidence is limited to qualitative zero-shot LAMBADA results on Pythia; the paper does not test prediction of downstream performance from pretraining loss or across a range of downstream tasks.
The note discusses dependence on setup and fitted interval, but does not compare fitting choices or empirically test how they change exponents or compute-optimal allocations.
